description: HEvOD: A database of hurricane evacuation orders in the United States is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Harsh Anand et al. Assessing and improving the effectiveness of evacuation orders can guide improvements in hurricane emergency response, particularly as the frequency of hurricanes increases in the United States. However, our understanding of causal relationships between evacuation orders and evacuation decision-making is still limited, in large part due to the lack of standardized, high-temporal-resolution data on historical evacuation orders. Coverage: national (US); published in 2024. Formats: Excel, CSV, JSON, Image, Python. The data are held in University of Virginia Dataverse and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 678660. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC0-1.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support emergency-service and public-facility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
